summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood inference performance vs baseline provider. Discussed p50/p95 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), batching, quantization impact, and next steps for staging run and security review.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: Okay welcome everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda - benchmark numbers up front, tuning recommendations, and then next steps.
00:12 Ravi Singh: Sounds good. appreciate it.
00:15 Priya Rao: Hi team, I'll take you through the slides briefly and then jump into the raw numbers. the spreadsheet link is in chat.
00:30 Sana Patel: I didn't get the link, can you drop again?
00:35 Priya Rao: Yep sending now. note - today's numbers compare Redwood running on H100 and A100 profiles vs our baseline provider (they call them CloudServe) on same VM sku. there are some env differences but we normalized as best we could.
00:50 Emily Johnson: Quick question - were the tests single-shot or streaming?
00:55 Priya Rao: Both. We ran burst tests for streaming generation (avg 512 token prompts) and synthetic throughput runs for batching (batch sizes 1,4,8,16).
01:08 Marcus Lee: ok show us the p95s. that's what ops cares about.
01:12 Priya Rao: Right - here's the headline: Redwood p50 for a 512-token generation (~chat response) on H100 was ~0.9s, p95 ~1.6s. On A100 p50 ~1.1s, p95 ~1.9s. Baseline provider p50 ~1.8s, p95 ~3.0s (same model family + 8-bit quant). so roughly 40-50% improvement at p95.
01:40 Ravi Singh: That's a big delta. how confident are we about the normalization? e.g., sequence length distribution?
01:47 Priya Rao: Good call - we used your anonymized production prompt set (500 prompts) and ran 5 repeats per config. sequence length median was 220 tokens, 95th was 480, so our 512 run approximates your 95th percentile. logs and raw traces included.
02:05 Alex Kim: Another thing - Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching + kv-cache for repeated context so the effective per-request latency drops for conversational workloads. in your tests we left kv-cache cold for the first pass, then warmed it for subsequent passes which is more realistic.
02:22 Sana Patel: For the warmed runs what numbers did you see?
02:25 Priya Rao: With warmed kv-cache on H100 p50 dropped to ~0.6s and p95 to ~1.1s. baseline provider doesn't have an equivalent kv-cache behavior in their managed offering so warmed gains were smaller.
02:38 Marcus Lee: throughput numbers? tokens/sec?
02:41 Priya Rao: Sure - synthetic throughput at batch=8 on H100: Redwood ~320 tokens/sec, baseline ~185 tokens/sec. On A100 Redwood ~260 tokens/sec. On batch=16 Redwood peaked ~380 tokens/sec but p95 latency goes up for single-request SLOs. so tradeoff there.
03:05 Emily Johnson: So for our latency-sensitive endpoints we should prefer smaller batches and warmed cache, got it. what's the cost delta if we pick H100 vs baseline?
03:14 Alex Kim: We estimated unit cost per 1M tokens: Redwood on shared hosted H100 profile ~ $X (note: ballpark) vs baseline provider their managed endpoint priced ~ 1.1-1.3x more per token once you factor in higher latency (more retries) and lower throughput. we'll send a detailed cost sheet.
03:31 Olivia Park: Procurement will need exact pricing and the SLA. also SOC2 and KMS details.
03:36 Daniel Ortiz: We'll attach SOC2 attestation, KMS integration doc, and SSO/SAML notes in the follow-up.
03:44 Ravi Singh: Any odd error modes or tail latency spikes?
03:48 Priya Rao: We saw occasional GC-ish stalls when running at very high batch concurrency on A100, which we isolated to the driver config; on H100 it's much more stable. also a few timeouts from the baseline provider in the warmed runs - they had retry churn.
04:05 Sana Patel: How reproducible are these numbers for our on-prem target? we might do private deployment.
04:11 Alex Kim: For Private deployments numbers depend on exact infra (GPU type, interconnect, NVMe). our Dedicated benchmarks map closely to the hosted H100 profiles; we can run a targeted on-prem suite if you share the hardware spec.
04:24 Marcus Lee: We'll share server spec this afternoon.
04:27 Priya Rao: Tuning notes: 1) enable continuous batching with max latency cap 150ms, 2) enable prefix kv-cache for sessions > 2 turns, 3) use 8-bit quantization for most models, 4) for aggressive cost savings test 4-bit but only with quality checks. these will be in the doc.
04:50 Ravi Singh: On quality: did you detect any generation regressions with 8-bit?
04:54 Priya Rao: Minimal. We ran automated eval on your eval set (NLG metrics + human spot-check). 8-bit had negligible quality delta for prompt types you run; 4-bit showed some deg in longer-context summarization - flagged those samples in the spreadsheet.
05:12 Emily Johnson: Great. Next steps from our side: run the 1k synthetic user staging test, share spec. From Redwood - send raw logs and tuning profile.
05:21 Alex Kim: Affirmative. also we should schedule the security deep dive - will include our security lead and solutions architect.
05:27 Olivia Park: Procurement wants NDA redlines and a contract skeleton.
05:30 Daniel Ortiz: We'll push NDA and skeleton to you by EOD Monday.
05:34 Ravi Singh: One more question - fallback behaviour if capacity constrained? baseline had auto-scaling but we saw higher latency spikes.
05:41 Priya Rao: Redwood supports smart routing + multi-variant fallbacks: can route to cheaper quant variant or fallback to dedicated pool. we've configured automatic fallback thresholds in the POC so you won't see large spikes. we'll show the routing telemetry in next call.
05:58 Sana Patel: minor transcript note - some names got auto-transcribed weirdly in earlier logs (CloudServe -> CloudServ).
06:03 Alex Kim: noted. we'll send cleaned logs and raw ones.
06:06 Ravi Singh: Ok thanks everyone. good progress.
06:10 Alex Kim: Recap - Alex will send full benchmark spreadsheet and logs; Priya will send tuning + quant profile; MediFlow will run staging test; schedule security review; procurement items to be shared. meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript contains some auto-transcription artifacts; timestamps approximate. raw benchmark CSV and perf traces attached in follow-up email (link).
